item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)

expect.asks_about: Whether cleanup means removing countertop clutter or changing the kitchen's appearance.

item.title: Clean Up This Kitchen
item.tests: Tests conservative interpretation of a vague cleanup request, clearing clutter without inventing a renovation.

answer_sheet.Meaning of cleanup: Clear the loose clutter off the counter, not a renovation.
answer_sheet.Permanent kitchen features: Keep the brown cabinets, beige tiles, counter material and existing kitchen layout.
answer_sheet.Style and size: Keep it a realistic photo with the same wide framing; free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: The countertop looks visibly tidier, with loose clutter removed.
The original brown wooden cabinets and beige tiles remain, rather than being replaced with renovated finishes.
The kitchen layout, fixed fixtures and viewpoint match the source.
Cleared counter areas look continuous and natural, without obvious erasure marks or floating object remnants.

turns.text: Can you clean up this pic? I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
Yes—before running anything, let’s define “clean up.”

Do you mean **remove the dishes, bottles, bags, and other counter clutter**, while keeping the cabinets, sinks, tiles, and layout unchanged? Or just improve the lighting, color, and sharpness?

**Lowest-cost listed option on your free plan:**
- One edited image, up to **640px**, using **Flux 2 Klein**
- Pricing **starts at 5 credits per image**; that’s the listed starting price, not a verified final quote
- No extra versions or upscaling

That’s already the smallest listed image-edit option. “Shorter” only applies to video; a simpler edit isn’t listed as cheaper.

**Nothing has run and no credits have been spent.** Tell me which cleanup you want, and I’ll keep generation paused until you approve the cost.
dialog.user: Clear the loose clutter off the counter—your call on which items—while keeping the brown cabinets, beige tiles, counter material, and kitchen layout unchanged, with the same realistic wide framing. For the single image up to 640px starting at 5 credits, ok, go ahead with that.

turns.agent:
The request was blocked by **insufficient credits**. No image was generated, and no generation credits were spent.

I used the approved single-image, 640px Flux 2 Klein option, listed from **5 credits**. There isn’t a cheaper or smaller image-edit setting listed, so I haven’t tried another run.

approvals.name: edit_image

style.prompt: Clean up this existing kitchen photograph by removing loose clutter from the countertops and sinks: loose dishes and plates, bottles, cans, bags, paper towels, sponges, cups, containers, and other small movable countertop items. Leave clean, naturally empty countertop surfaces, reconstructing the original counter material realistically where items were removed. Preserve the brown wooden cabinets, cabinet hardware, beige tiled backsplash, counter material, all sinks and faucets, window, kitchen architecture and layout exactly as in the source. Keep the original camera position, entire wide framing, perspective, proportions, realistic photographic appearance and natural lighting. Do not remodel, replace surfaces, add decor, crop, or reframe.
